skill_layout.pattern: skills/<root>/<skill-name>/SKILL.md (uppercase required for codex/etc; claude root also accepts legacy lowercase skill.md, normalized to SKILL.md on install)
optional_per_skill_resources: <skill>/agents/openai.yaml (codex root only, generated UI metadata, e.g. skills/codex/kiwi-hot-fix/agents/openai.yaml)
<skill>/references/extended-workflow.md (codex and etc roots, progressive-disclosure split when SKILL.md > 500 lines; not present in skills/claude source)
skill_layout..speckiwi-skill-install.json: Only present under installed DESTINATION dirs (.agents/skills/<name>/.speckiwi-skill-install.json), never under skills/claude|codex|etc source dirs. Written by src/core/skills/install-skill.ts:495-527 buildInstallMetadata(); field installMode is literally 'generated-runtime-mirror' (line 512).

mirror_roots.skills/claude: Hand-authored canonical source for the Claude agent target. Referenced as SOURCE_ROOT_BY_AGENT.claude in src/core/skills/install-skill.ts:31-36.
mirror_roots.skills/codex: Hand-maintained, semantically rewritten mirror for the Codex agent target (uppercase SKILL.md, two-field frontmatter only, progressive-disclosure references/, generated agents/openai.yaml). Documented in skills/codex/MIGRATION_PLAN.md:1-218. Diffed against skills/claude/kiwi-srs-sync: only SKILL.md content differs plus added agents/ and references/ dirs.
mirror_roots.skills/etc: Hand-maintained mirror for opencode/hermes agent targets (SOURCE_ROOT_BY_AGENT.opencode = 'etc', SOURCE_ROOT_BY_AGENT.hermes = 'etc' at install-skill.ts:31-36). Same references/ pattern as codex but no agents/openai.yaml.
mirror_roots..agents/skills: NOT a source root. It is the project-scope INSTALLED destination for agent='codex' (install-skill.ts:204-208: case 'codex' -> path.join(projectRoot,'.agents','skills')). Generated by `speckiwi skills install codex <name>` / `skills add`; content is a byte-copy of skills/codex/<name>/* plus the .speckiwi-skill-install.json manifest. Also .claude/skills (agent=claude) and .opencode/skills (agent=opencode) are valid install destinations per install-skill.ts:198-214 but do not currently exist in this repo checkout.

canonical_root: skills/claude is the primary hand-authored baseline per skills/codex/MIGRATION_PLAN.md:5-7 ('The Claude source tree remains the baseline and must not be edited during Codex migration unless the user asks for a source-side change'). skills/codex and skills/etc are derived, agent-specific rewrites of that baseline (not auto-generated by a script — maintained by manual/agent-driven migration passes). .agents/skills (and the other install destinations) are pure generated runtime mirrors, never hand-edited (installed metadata sets noManualEdit: true, install-skill.ts:526).

installer.cli_commands: speckiwi skills install <agent> <name|all> [--scope project|global|--dest <path>] [--category <name>] [--dry-run] [--json]; alias `skills add` (see test/cli/skills-cli.test.ts:16-56)
installer.no_manifest_of_skill_names: resolveSkillNames() with selector='all' (install-skill.ts:184-196) dynamically reads the source root directory listing and includes any subdirectory (not prefixed with '_') that has a supported SKILL.md/skill.md entrypoint. There is NO static list a new skill must be added to for install/copy purposes — dropping a new skills/claude/<name>/SKILL.md folder in is enough for the installer to discover it.
installer.packaging: package.json 'files' field (package.json:37-44) ships whole directories 'skills/codex', 'skills/claude', 'skills/etc' verbatim in the npm tarball; a new skill folder is automatically packaged without any package.json edit. '.agents/skills' is NOT in 'files' (it is a per-project generated artifact, not shipped).

frontmatter_convention.rule: YAML frontmatter must contain ONLY name and description (skills/codex/MIGRATION_PLAN.md:66, :101-104). install-skill.ts:648-659 parseFrontmatter() only extracts/requires 'name'; it must exactly equal the containing folder name (install-skill.ts:325-327, :294-296, :623) or the source/install is rejected with SKILL_INSTALL_INVALID_SOURCE / SKILL_INSTALL_FAILED.
frontmatter_convention.description_conventions: Single long string embedding: (1) a plain-language summary of the workflow/topology, (2) a bullet-like '트리거 —' (trigger) list of literal phrases including Korean and English variants and slash-style ('kiwi hot fix', '핫픽스', 'hotfix', 'urgent fix', ...), (3) supported CLI-style flags with their effect ('--mini 로 비용 절감...', '--auto 로 사용자 게이트 자동 진행...'). Examples: skills/claude/kiwi-hot-fix/SKILL.md:3, skills/claude/kiwi-srs-sync/SKILL.md:3. Codex versions rewrite the same fields into English with 'Use for <trigger list>. Supports --flag1, --flag2, ...' phrasing (skills/codex/kiwi-hot-fix/SKILL.md:3).
frontmatter_convention.no_changelog_rule: Global org/user rule (CLAUDE.md §7, and mirrored inside skill bodies themselves) forbids a changelog section in skill files. Confirmed self-referencing line inside an actual skill: skills/claude/kiwi-pm/SKILL.md:29 — '§0.10 CLAUDE.md §6 시그니처 금지 + §7 변경 이력 금지. 본 스킬 본문에 `## 변경 이력` / `## Changelog` / `### v0.x.y` 섹션 없음 — git history 가 SSOT.' A leading '# <skill-name> v0.1.2' style version header (e.g. skills/claude/kiwi-srs-sync/SKILL.md:6) is a current-state marker, not a changelog, and is allowed.

skill_tests.asserts: Runs `npm pack --dry-run --json` and asserts the resulting file list contains specific literal paths such as 'skills/codex/kiwi-pm/SKILL.md', 'skills/claude/kiwi-review-fix-loop/SKILL.md', 'skills/etc/kiwi-hot-fix/SKILL.md'. This is a spot-check of a subset of skills, not exhaustive; a brand-new skill is NOT automatically required to be added here, but doing so for kiwi-step would follow the established per-skill spot-check pattern.

End-to-end: `npm pack` -> install tarball into a scratch project -> run installed CLI `doctor --json` and assert doctorReport.checks contains an objectContaining({ id: 'packed-skill-entrypoints', status: 'pass' }); then runs `skills install opencode kiwi-pm --dest ...` and asserts the installed SKILL.md contains 'name: kiwi-pm'.

NOT a test file but the authoritative registry a new skill must be added to. EXPECTED_KIWI_SKILLS is a hardcoded array of the 13 current kiwi-* skill names; EXPECTED_SKILL_ENTRYPOINTS (line 74) expands it to 'skills/{codex,claude,etc}/{skill}/SKILL.md' (39 paths). The 'packed-skill-entrypoints' doctor check (lines 158-166) only verifies these LISTED paths exist — it never fails for skills present on disk but absent from the list, so omitting kiwi-step from EXPECTED_KIWI_SKILLS would silently NOT verify its packaging via doctor.

Runs runPackageDoctor() against a fixture workspace and asserts report.checks contains expect.objectContaining({ id: 'packed-skill-entrypoints', status: 'pass' }) via arrayContaining — this is the closest thing to a red/green TDD hook for a new skill: adding 'kiwi-step' to EXPECTED_KIWI_SKILLS (src/doctor/package-doctor.ts) before creating the 3 SKILL.md files will fail this check (missingSkillFiles non-empty -> status 'fail' -> report.ok false), and creating the files makes it pass.

Generic installer mechanics only, using synthetic temp-directory fixture skills (writeSkill() helper writes a throwaway 'kiwi-pm' style skill under a tmp root, skills-cli.test.ts:16-24). These tests validate install/update/skip/conflict semantics, entrypoint normalization (skill.md -> SKILL.md), frontmatter identity checks, and CLI usage-error codes. They do NOT read or assert on any real skills/claude|codex|etc content, so they require no changes for a new real skill.

runtime_ops.name: claim_step
runtime_ops.surface: MCP tool only, no dedicated CLI command
runtime_ops.schema: src/mcp/server.ts:406-413 (step: string, touchesScope: string, touchesReq: string[], force?: boolean, supersede?: string, dryRun?: boolean)
runtime_ops.schema_registry_note: src/mcp/schemas.ts:381-388 — the tool is piggybacked on the 'set-supersede' ToolSpec entry with an explicit comment: 'set-supersede: real CLI mutation; also hosts the v3 claim_step MCP tool (no dedicated CLI).' Confirmed no 'claim' CLI command exists in src/cli/commands/mutations.ts or src/cli/index.ts.
runtime_ops.behavior: Appends a row to docs/spec/steps/state.md declaring step/touchesScope/touchesReq. Two-stage write-skew gate: direct same-REQ intersection with another active step -> hard-block STEP_DIRECT_CONFLICT (unforceable); transitive-only overlap via depends_on closure -> soft-block STEP_OVERLAP unless force=true (then pins an '<!-- overlaps: ... -->' marker); supersede target that is verified/frozen -> STEP_SUPERSEDE_PROTECTED.
runtime_ops.operational_implication_for_FR-FLOW-014: Because claim_step has no CLI fallback, kiwi-step's AC-1 (claim before authoring) can only be satisfied when speckiwi MCP is actually available; if MCP is down there is no degraded/CLI path and the skill must halt rather than proceed with a CLI substitute.
